source_proof_observations: Chapter 4 includes proofs of the general stationary-iteration spectral-radius criterion and diagonal-dominance convergence tests.
Chapter 6 was read in full, including the exact-arithmetic Arnoldi/GMRES/CG derivations, convergence bounds, and the discussion of loss of Lanczos/CG orthogonality in finite precision.
Chapter 9 was read in full, including left/right/split preconditioning derivations and flexible GMRES optimality.
Chapter 10 was read in full, including ILU(0), ILU(p), ILUT, approximate inverse, and block preconditioner material; its claims are not imported as local proofs.

Chapter 13 was read in full, including the Galerkin projector argument, the smoothing-plus-approximation two-grid estimate, the FMG assumptions and proof, complexity recurrences, and the heuristic scope of AMG.

source_proof_observations: The bounded lecture packet 31–35 and 37 was read completely. Lecture 31 derives the splitting and exact spectral-radius criterion, then Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel/SOR; lecture 32–33 analyze the Poisson model problem and work counts; lectures 34–35 derive polynomial/Krylov and CG/Lanczos structure; lecture 37 gives the exact-arithmetic CG Chebyshev bound and GMRES residual characterization.

The additional eigenvalue notes were read completely. They give the stated power/shift/subspace/QR hypotheses and convergence mechanisms; lecture 38–39 explicitly separates exact Lanczos from floating-point orthogonality loss and gives a Ritz residual identity and extremal Ritz estimate.
These are lecture notes, not a blanket formal proof certificate. The research packet records the scope and treatment of each claim and does not infer a proof merely from the course citation.

sources.citation: N. Halko, P.-G. Martinsson, and J. A. Tropp, “Finding Structure with Randomness: Probabilistic Algorithms for Constructing Approximate Matrix Decompositions,” SIAM Review 53 (2011), no. 2, 217–288; arXiv:0909.4061v2 (14 Dec 2010).
sources.license_and_access: Public arXiv full-text preprint. No open reuse license is asserted here; the full-text cache is kept only in the ignored scratchpad source directory.
sources.reading_status: Complete reading of the full 74-page PDF, including algorithms, proofs, numerical examples, appendix, and references.

actual_reading_ranges.article_printed_pages: The preprint body is numbered pp. 1–74; the published SIAM Review pagination is 217–288.

source_proof_observations: The deterministic range-finder bound (Theorem 9.1) and power inequality (Theorem 9.2) are proved in the source.

The expected and high-probability range-finder theorems have detailed derivations in §§10 and Appendix A, but their arguments rely on Gaussian matrix norm, pseudoinverse, and concentration facts that are stated or cited without complete proofs in this source.
The pseudoinverse Frobenius moment and tail arguments are developed in Appendix A. Some pseudoinverse spectral-norm estimates rely on Chen–Dongarra rather than a proof in the read paper.

The SRFT subspace embedding theorem (Theorem 11.1) is stated but its proof is explicitly omitted as a variation of another source. The SRFT matrix-error theorem (Theorem 11.2) is proved conditionally on that result.
The a-posteriori Gaussian norm estimator is stated in §4.3 with its proof pointed to another source; that proof is not included here.

The error theorems assume exact arithmetic and probability over the specified independent random test matrix. §4.5 explicitly warns that raw power iteration loses small singular modes to roundoff and recommends QR orthonormalization between applications.
